procnotices.bid_description: Equipping of Exploratory Boreholes Project-Lot 1- Sarman - Tarbaj Water Supply
procnotices.contact_organization: Northern Water Works Development Agency
procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR BIDS (RFB)

 

Country: Kenya

 

Project:  WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT

 

Credit No.: IDA-60300

 

Ref: KE-NWWDA-541055-CW-RFB

 

 

RFB Title: Equipping of Exploratory Boreholes Project-Lot 1- Sarman - Tarbaj Water Supply

 

County

 

 

Contract No. KE. KE-NWWDA-541055-CW-RFB

 

  1. The Northern Water Works Development Agency has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Water and Sanitation Development Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Equipping of Exploratory Boreholes Project-Lot 1- Sarman - Tarbaj Water Supply, Contract No. KE-NWWDA-541055-CW-RFB.

 

  1. The Northern Water Works Development Agency now invites sealed bids from eligible bidders for Equipping of Exploratory Boreholes Project-Lot 1- Sarman - Tarbaj Water Supply, Contract No. KE-NWWDA-541055-CW-RFB, as detailed below:, , 160/140 OD, PN10-16, and associated civil works

  

  • Borehole Equipping with Solar.
  • HDPE Rising Main 40KM , 160/140 OD, PN10-16, and associated civil works
  1. Bidding will be conducted through the National Competitive Bidding procurement using a Request for Bids as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations” for IPF Borrower and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the procurement Regulations.

 

 

  1. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from Northern Water Works Development Agency, Procurement office (A3 Ground floor), email info@nwwda.go.ke  and inspect the bidding documents during office hours 00900 to 1600 hours at the address given below

 

  1. The bidding document in English may be downloaded free  of charge from our website www.nwwda.go.ke or www.tenders.go.ke - Public Procurement Information Portal Addendum/Clarifications will also be posted in the NWWDA website immediately they become available

 

  1. Bids must be delivered  to the address below on or before the 12th May 2026 at 11.00 am. Electronic bidding will not be permitted. Late bids will be rejected. Bids will be publicly opened in the presence of the bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who choose to attend at the address below at Conference Room, at 11.30 am on 12th May 2026.
  2. All Bids shall be accompanied by a Bid Security (Unconditional Bank guarantee) of Kshs. 2,000,000.00 (Two Million  only)
  3. The address referred to above is:

 

 

Chief Executive Officer

Northern Water Works Development Agency

Maji House, Kismayu Road

P.O. Box 495 – 70100

GARISSA, KENYA

Fax: +254-46-2103598

Info@nwwda.go.ke

Website: www.nwwda.go.ke

SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Country:   Kenya

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.:  60300KE

RFB Reference No.: KIMAWASCO-481608-GO-RFB

1.      The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Supply and Delivery of AMR enabled Customer water meters (DN15mm & DN20mm) Contract No. KE-KIMAWASCO -481608-GO-RFB

2.      The Kilifi Mariakani Water and Sewerage Company limited (KIMAWASCO now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for Supply and Delivery of AMR enabled Customer Water Meters (DN15mm & DN 20mm). The contract shall comprise of the following;

REQUEST FOR QUOTATION

 

COUNTRY: KENYA

 

PROJECT:  WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSDP)

 

Credit No: IDA-60300

 

 

RFQ TITLE: PROCUREMENT OF WATER METER FITTINGS & INSTALLATION OF EXISTING WATER METERS IN STORE 4266 IN NUMBER.

 

Ref No: KE-GAWASCO-472825-GO-RFQ

 

  1. This RFQ is for the procurement of Goods: Procurement of water meter fittings & Installation of existing water meters in store 4266 in number and required by Garissa Water and Sewerage Company Ltd (GAWASCO). It is subject to accelerated emergency procurement procedures.
  2. The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank (Bank) toward the cost of the purchase of and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Procurement of water meter fittings & Installation of existing water meters in store 4266 in number
  3. The Garissa Water and Sewerage Company Ltd (GAWASCO), now invites quotations from suppliers for the Goods Procurement of water meter fittings & Installation of existing water meters in store 4266 in number . described in Annex 1: Purchaser’s Requirements, attached to this RFQ.

Fraud and Corruption

  1. The Bank requires compliance with the Bank’s Anti-Corruption Guidelines and its prevailing sanctions policies and procedures as set forth in the WBG’s Sanctions Framework, as set forth in the attachment to the Contract Conditions (Attachment A).
  2. In further pursuance of this policy, Suppliers shall permit and shall cause their agents (where declared or not), subcontractors, sub-consultants, service providers, suppliers, and personnel, to permit the Bank to inspect all accounts, records and other documents relating to the RFQ and contract performance (in the case of award), and to have them audited by auditors appointed by the Bank.

Eligible Goods All the Goods to be supplied under the Contract and financed by the Bank may have their origin in any country in accordance with Para. 10.

Eligible Suppliers

  1. In case the Supplier is a joint venture (JV), all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the execution of the entire Contract in accordance with the Contract terms. The JV shall nominate a representative who shall have the authority to conduct all business for and on behalf of any and all the members of the JV during the Request for Quotations process and, in the event the JV is awarded the Contract, during contract execution.
  2. A Supplier may have the nationality of any country, subject to the restrictions pursuant to para. 9 and 10 hereinafter. A Supplier shall be deemed to have the nationality of a country if the Supplier is constituted, incorporated or registered in, and operates in conformity with, the provisions of the laws of that country, as evidenced by its articles of incorporation (or equivalent documents of constitution or association) and its registration documents, as the case may be. This criterion also shall apply to the determination of the nationality of proposed subcontractors or subconsultants for any part of the Contract including Related Services.
  3. Firms and individuals may be ineligible if so indicated in para. 10 below and:
      1. as a matter of law or official regulations, the Borrower’s country prohibits commercial relations with that country, provided that the Bank is satisfied that such exclusion does not preclude effective competition for the supply of Goods or the contracting of works or services required; or
      2. by an act of compliance with a decision of the United Nations Security Council taken under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations, the Borrower’s country prohibits any import of Goods or contracting of works or services from that country, or any payments to any country, person, or entity in that country.
  4. In reference to paras. 6 and 8, for the information of suppliers, at the present time firms, goods and services from the following countries are excluded from this procurement process:
      1. Under para. 6 and 9 (a): [insert a list of the countries following approval by the Bank to apply the restriction or state: none.
      2. Under para. 6 and 9 (b): none
  5. A Supplier that has been sanctioned by the Bank, pursuant to the Bank’s Anti-Corruption Guidelines, in accordance with its prevailing sanctions policies and procedures as set forth in the WBG’s Sanctions Framework as described in the attachment to the Contract Conditions (Attachment A) paragraph 2.2 d., shall be ineligible to submit Quotations or be awarded or otherwise benefit from a Bank-financed contract, financially or otherwise, during such period of time as the Bank shall have determined.  A list of debarred firms and individuals is available on the Bank’s external website: http://www.worldbank.org/debarr.
  6. Suppliers that are state-owned enterprises or institutions in the Purchaser’s country may be eligible to compete and be awarded a Contract(s) only if they can establish, in a manner acceptable to the Bank, that they:
      1. are legally and financially autonomous;
      2. operate under commercial law; and
      3. are not under supervision of the Purchaser.
  7. A Supplier shall not have a conflict of interest. Any Supplier found to have a conflict of interest shall be disqualified. A Supplier may be considered to have a conflict of interest for the purpose of this Request for Quotations process, if the Supplier:
      1. directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by or is under common control with another Supplier that submitted a Quotation;
      2. receives or has received any direct or indirect subsidy from another Supplier that submitted a Quotation;
      3. has the same legal representative as another Supplier that submitted a Quotation;
      4. has a relationship with another Supplier that submitted a Quotation, directly or through common third parties, that puts it in a position to influence the Quotation of another Supplier, or influence the decisions of the Purchaser regarding this Request for Quotations process; or

SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE

INVITATION FOR BIDS

COUNTRY: KENYA

PROJECT: WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSDP)

CREDIT NO: 60300 –KE

IFB TITLE & CONTRACT No.

 

  1. KE-TAVEVO-451075-CW-RFB - Construction And Completion Of 8No. Ablution Blocks At Voi, Mwatate, Maungu, Bura, Taveta And Wundanyi Towns; and
  2. KE-TAVEVO-449427-CW-RFB - Proposed Construction Of An Office Block For TAVEVO Water & Sewerage Company Ltd.

 

The Government of Kenya through the Ministry of Water & Sanitation and Irrigation (MoWSI) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contracts for “Construction And Completion Of 8No. Ablution Blocks At Voi, Mwatate, Maungu, Bura, Taveta And Wundanyi Towns and Proposed Construction Of An Office Block For TAVEVO Water & Sewerage Company Ltd.

 

TAVEVO Water and Sewerage Company Limited, a Water Service Provider licensed by Water Services Regulatory Board (WASREB) and fully owned by the County Government of Taita Taveta now invites sealed bids from eligible and qualified bidders to undertake the works. The works include:

 

S/N

Tender Ref No.

Tender Description

Location

Construction Period

1.

KE-TAVEVO-451075-CW-RFB

Construction And Completion Of 8No. Ablution Blocks At Voi, Mwatate, Maungu,Bura Taveta And Wundanyi Towns

TAVEVO Water and Sewerage Company Limited, Sophia Road Opposite Ministry of Agriculture Offices.

8 - (EIGHT) months construction period following the date of effectiveness of the Contract

2.

KE-TAVEVO-449427-CW-RFB

Proposed Construction Of An Office Block For TAVEVO Water & Sewerage Company Ltd

TAVEVO Water and Sewerage Company Limited, Sophia Road Opposite Ministry of Agriculture Offices.

6 - (SIX) months construction period following the date of effectiveness of the Contract

 

Bidding will be conducted through National Competitive Bidding procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Guidelines: Procurement of Goods, Works and Non-Consulting Services under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants by World Bank Borrowers Dated January 2011 and Revised in July, 2014  (“Procurement Guidelines) and is open to all eligible bidders as defined in the Procurement Guidelines. In addition, please refer to paragraphs 1.6 and 1.7 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Interested eligible bidders may obtain further information from at the address given below and inspect the bidding documents during office hours (0800hrs- 1300hrs & 1400hrs to 1700hrs) from Monday to Friday except on public Holiday.

 

A complete set of bidding documents in English may be downloaded free of charge from the company website: www.tavevowater.co.ke and Public Procurement Information Portal (PPIP). Bidders who download the bidding document must forward their particulars immediately to procurement@tavevowater.co.ke to facilitate any further clarification or addendum.

 

Completed bidding document should be submitted in a plain sealed outer envelope enclosing separately sealed envelopes (in “ORIGINAL” and “COPY”) clearly marked Contract Reference Number and Contract Tittle and must be delivered to the address below on or before THURSDAY, 5TH DECEMBER, 2024 at 1100hrs Local Time. Electronic bidding will not be permitted. Late bids will be rejected. Bids will be publicly opened in the presence of the bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who choose to attend at the address below on THURSDAY, 5TH DECEMBER, 2024 at 1100hrs.

All Bids shall be valid until 3RD APRIL, 2025 (119 days) from the date of bid submission and shall be accompanied by a Bid security only issued by a bank licensed by Central Bank of Kenya as Follows: -

  1. KE-TAVEVO-451075-CW-RFB - Construction And Completion Of 8No. Ablution Blocks At Voi, Mwatate, Maungu, Taveta And Wundanyi Towns – KSHS. 1,500,000.00 (Kenya Shillings One Million Five Hundred Thousand Only); and

Bid Security shall remain valid for a further 28 days beyond the bid validity period (1ST MAY, 2025). 

The address referred to above is:

 

The Managing Director,

VOI, KENYA

CONTRACT TITLE:  Construction of Sludge Treatment Facilities in Kilifi and Mtwapa Towns

REFERENCE NO.:  KE-KIMAWASCO-416959-CW-RFB

1.   The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Construction of Sludge Treatment Facilities in Kilifi and Mtwapa Towns, Contract No. KE-KIMAWASCO-416959-CW-RFB.

2.   The Kilifi Mariakani Water and Sewerage Company limited (KIMAWASCO) now invites sealed bids from eligible bidders for Construction of Sludge Treatment Facilities in Kilifi and Mtwapa Towns. The construction period is 9 months and defects liability period is12 months. The scope of works comprises the following:

  1. Construction of 2Nr Sludge Treatment Facilities (1Nr in Kilifi and 1Nr in Mtwapa) each comprising of.
  • 1Nr Exhauster Discharge Bay
  • 1Nr Equalization Tank (18 m3 Capacity)
  • 1Nr Anaerobic Baffled Reactor (Twin – 95m³ Capacity)
  • 1Nr Facultative Pond (29m x 13m x 2m at Top Embankment)
  • 2Nr Constructed Wetlands (18m x 6m each)
  • 8Nr Sludge Drying Beds (13m x 10m - Plan Dimensions)
  • 1Nr Operator’s Offices / Guard House
  • Site and Ancillary Works including Soak Pit, Fencing, Internal Roads, Surface Drainage, etc.
  1. Supply of 2 Nr. Sewage exhausters each 7m3 capacity

      More details are contained in the bidding documents.

3.   Bidding will be conducted through the  National Competitive Bidding (NCB) procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Guidelines: Procurement of Goods, Works and Non-Consulting Services under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants by World Bank Borrowers of January 2011, revised in July 2014, and is open to all eligible bidders as defined in the Procurement Guidelines. In addition, please refer to paragraphs 1.6 and 1.7 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

4.   Interested eligible bidders may obtain further information from Kilifi Mariakani Water and Sewerage Company Limited during office hours from 0900 to 1700 hours from Monday to Friday, excluding lunch hour (1300 to1400 hours) and public holidays at the address given below.

5.   A complete set of bidding documents in English language may be purchased by interested eligible bidders upon the submission of a written application to the address below and upon payment of a non-refundable fee of Kshs.1000 per set. The method of payment will be through Banker’s cheque payable to Kilifi Mariakani Water and Sewerage Company Limited. Bidders can access the bidding documents at our website and download for free.   Bidders who download the bidding documents are required to notify the purchaser by email with full contact details that they intend to participate; this will facilitate issuance of notifications by the purchaser to all bidders where necessary. The Bidding Documents will be collected from the address below upon production of a purchase receipt. No arrangements have been made for other methods of delivery of bidding documents.

6.   Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before 1115hrs on 30th May,2024. Electronic bidding will not be permitted. The bids must be clearly marked “Construction of Sludge Treatment Facilities in Kilifi and Mtwapa Towns -Contract No. KE-KIMAWASCO-416959-CW-RFB”.

Late bids will be rejected. Bids will be publicly opened in the presence of the bidders or the bidders’ designated representatives at the address below on 30th May, 2024 at 1115hrs.

7.  All bids must be accompanied by a Bid Security (unconditional bank guarantee) of; Kshs. 1,500,000 (Kenya Shillings One Million, Five Hundred Thousand Only) and

8.  Pre-Bid meeting shall take place at KIMAWASCO head offices in Kilifi Town Off-Mombasa Malindi Road at former KDDP Offices on 26th April, 2024 at 1000Hrs.

procnotices.notice_text:
SPECIFIC PROCUREMENT NOTICE

COUNTRY:                          Kenya

NAME OF PROJECT:         Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP)

LOAN NO./CREDIT NO./ GRANT NO: 60300 KE

CONTRACT TITLE: Construction of Sludge Treatment Facilities in Kilifi and Mtwapa Towns

REFERENCE NO.:  KE-KIMAWASCO-377450-CW-RFB

1.     The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards payments under the contract for Construction of Sludge Treatment Facilities in Kilifi and Mtwapa Towns, Contract No. KE-KIMAWASCO-377450-CW-RFB.

2.     The Kilifi Mariakani Water and Sewerage Company limited (KIMAWASCO) now invites sealed bids from eligible bidders for Construction of Sludge Treatment Facilities in Kilifi and Mtwapa Towns. The construction period is 9 months and Defects Liability Period is 12 months. The scope of works comprises the following:

  1. Construction of 2Nr Sludge Treatment Facilities (1Nr in Kilifi and 1Nr in Mtwapa) each comprising of.
  • 1Nr Exhauster Discharge Bay
  • 1Nr Equalization Tank (32m³ Capacity)
  • 1Nr Anaerobic Baffled Reactor (Twin – 95m³ Capacity)
  • 1Nr Facultative Pond (29m x 13m x 2m at Top Embankment)
  • 2Nr Constructed Wetlands (18m x 6m each)
  • 8Nr Sludge Drying Beds (13m x 10m - Plan Dimensions)
  • 1Nr Soak pit
  • Site and Ancillary Works including 1Nr Operator’s Offices / Guard House, Fencing, Internal Roads, Surface Drainage, etc.
  1. Supply of 2 Nr. Sewage exhausters each 7m3 capacity

      More details are contained in the bidding documents.

3.     Bidding will be conducted through the  National Competitive Bidding (NCB) procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Guidelines: Procurement of Goods, Works and Non-Consulting Services under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants by World Bank Borrowers of January 2011, revised in July 2014, and is open to all eligible bidders as defined in the Procurement Guidelines. In addition, please refer to paragraphs 1.6 and 1.7 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

4.     Interested eligible bidders may obtain further information from Kilifi Mariakani Water and Sewerage Company Limited during office hours from 0900 to 1700 hours from Monday to Friday, excluding lunch hour (1300 to1400 hours) and public holidays at the address given below.

5.     A complete set of bidding documents in English language may be purchased by interested eligible bidders upon the submission of a written application to the address below and upon payment of a non-refundable fee of Kshs.1000 per set. The method of payment will be through Banker’s cheque payable to Kilifi Mariakani Water and Sewerage Company Limited. Bidders can access the bidding documents at our website and download for free.   Bidders who download the bidding documents are required to notify the purchaser by email with full contact details that they intend to participate; this will facilitate issuance of notifications by the purchaser to all bidders where necessary. The Bidding Documents will be collected from the address below upon production of a purchase receipt. No arrangements have been made for other methods of delivery of bidding documents.

6.     Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before 06th October,2023. Electronic bidding will not be permitted. The bids must be clearly marked “Construction of Sludge Treatment Facilities in Kilifi and Mtwapa Towns -Contract No. KE-KIMAWASCO-377450-CW-RFB”. Late bids will be rejected. Bids will be publicly opened in the presence of the bidders or the bidders’ designated representatives at the address below on 06th October, at 1115hrs.

7.     All bids must be accompanied by a Bid Security (unconditional bank guarantee) of;

        Kshs. 1,500,000 (Kenya Shillings One Million, Five Hundred Thousand Only) and

8.     Pre-Bid meeting shall take place at KIMAWASCO head offices in Kilifi Town Off-Mombasa Malindi Road at former KDDP Offices on 05th September,2023 at 1000hrs.

procnotices.bid_description: Procurement of a Communication Specialist
procnotices.contact_organization: Ministry of Water and Irrigation
procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIC OF KENYA

MINISTRY OF WATER, SANITATION AND IRRIGATION

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

COUNTRY: KENYA

 

NAME OF PROJECT: WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSDP)

PROJECT No.: P156634

CREDIT No. 6030 -KE

 

Assignment Title: INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT -  COMMUNICATION SPECIALIST

 

CONTRACT REF. No.: KE-MOWI-249824-CS-INDV

 

The Government of the Republic of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for consulting Services for a Communication Specialist to lead all communication activities for the project.

 

  1. The Project comprises four components; -
  1. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in the coastal region, - Mombasa, Kwale, Kilifi and Taita Taveta Counties
  2. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in Wajir and Garissa Counties
  3. National performance-based financing (PBF) that includes support for water and sanitation infrastructure investments, and technical assistance for performance-based financing.
  4. Project management to finance the management activities associated with project implementation.

 

  1. The main objective of this consultancy is to assist the Project Coordinator (PC), through specific component heads in the exercise of PC’s strategic management duties in relation to all aspects of project communication.

 

  1. This is a full-time post up to project closure. However, the Communication Specialist shall be engaged on a one-year renewable contract subject to satisfactory performance and availability of funds and continuation of the project.

 

  1. Interested candidates can access the detailed Terms of Reference for this assignment on the Ministry’s website: www.water@go.ke.

 

  1. Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation now invites eligible individual consultants to express their interest (EOI) in providing these services. Interested consultants must provide their CVs and information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

 

  1. The desired consultant must be in possession of the following qualifications and experience: -
  1. A master’s degree in development communication, Journalism, public relations, or related field.
  2. Over 8 years of demonstrable experience working as a communication Specialist on projects, especially donor funded. Experience on World Bank funded projects will be an added advantage.
  3. Demonstrate a good understanding of the complexities of development work in Kenya. Experience in the water sector is an added advantage
  4. Excellent knowledge and experience on the use of traditional and new media tools for communication and dissemination
  5. Excellent knowledge of media landscape in Kenya
  6. Ability to work in a multi-disciplinary team environment (National and County Governments).
  7. Capability and proven experience in crafting messages in various formats (press releases, websites, success stories, tweets, etc.) targeting a variety of audiences.
  8. Excellent editorial, written and verbal communication skills.

(The applicant MUST provide a sample portfolio of communication work done, accompanying their resume and cover letter. Sample portfolio may be in the form of videos, stories, documentaries etc.)

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers, January 2011 revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

  1. Selection of the Individual Consultant will be in accordance with World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers, January 2011 revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”). The selection criteria will be solely based on individual experience and qualifications.

 

  1. Interested Individual Consultants may obtain further necessary information at the address below during office hours between 0900 to 1600 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400Hrs) and public holidays.

 

  1. The expressions of interest in written form must be delivered in person, or by mail to the address below so as to reach by 28th September, 2021 at 11:00am. EOI may also be deposited in the Tender Box on Ground Floor, Maji House, Ngong Road and must be clearly marked: “CONTRACT No: KE-MOWI-249824-CS-INDV FOR A COMMUNICATION SPECIALIST” addressed to:

Project Coordinator

Water and Sanitation Development Project,

Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation

Maji House, 5th Floor – Room No. 511, Ngong Road, Nairobi,

Tel: +254 02 2716103 Ext. 42234

procnotices.bid_description: Consultancy to undertake an inventory of existing rural water supply systems, O&M institutional capacity and community water vulnerability and needs assessments in five ASAL counties of Kenya (Turkana, Marsabit, Mandera, Wajir, and Garissa)
procnotices.contact_organization: Ministry of Water and Irrigation
procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIC OF KENYA

MINISTRY OF WATER, SANITATION AND IRRIGATION

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)

COUNTRY: KENYA

 

NAME OF PROJECT: WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSDP)

PROJECT No.: P156634

CREDIT No. 6030 -KE

 

Assignment Title: CONSULTANCY TO UNDERTAKE AN INVENTORY OF EXISTING RURAL WATER SUPPLY SYSTEMS, O&M INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY AND COMMUNITY WATER VULNERABILITY AND NEEDS ASSESSMENTS IN FIVE ASAL COUNTIES OF KENYA (TURKANA, MARSABIT, MANDERA, WAJIR AND GARISSA)

 

CONTRACT REF. No.: KE-MOWI-246482-CS-QCBS

 

The Government of the Republic of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for consulting services to undertake an inventory of rural water supply systems in five ASAL counties.

 

  1. The Project comprises four components; -
  1. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in the coastal region, - Mombasa, Kwale, Kilifi and Taita Taveta Counties
  2. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in Wajir and Garissa Counties
  3. National performance-based financing (PBF) that includes support for water and sanitation infrastructure investments, and technical assistance for performance-based financing.
  4. Project management to finance the management activities associated with project implementation.

 

  1. The main objective of this consultancy is to assess the location, conditions, operational status, the O&M capacity and the administrative arrangements at each rural Water Supply Scheme (WSS) and strategic drought-contingency boreholes in five ASAL counties of Turkana, Marsabit, Mandera, Wajir, and Garissa. It will also establish the extent of rehabilitation requirements, preliminary cost estimates for prioritized WSSs rehabilitation and to strengthen the strategic drought-contingency boreholes network as well as make recommendations to streamline their sustainability.

 

  1. The duration of the assignment is six (6) months.
  2. The Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation now invites eligible consultants to express their interest (EOI) in providing these services. Interested consultants must provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

 

  1. The desired consultant must be in possession of the following qualifications and experience: -
  1. Relevance and suitability of the core business area of the applicant firm with the subject assignment; Core business must demonstrate capacity to undertake analysis of institutional models for the design, operation, and maintenance of  rural Water Supply Schemes in Kenya or in countries with similar characteristics as Kenya.
  2. Firm should have at least five (5) years relevant experience in advising governments and major International Financial Institutions’ financed projects/programs on rural water supply services policies, strategies, plans and implementations. (Relevant completion certificates and/or letters of recommendation from previous assignments to be provided).
  3. Firm should have undertaken at least one (1) similar assignment in the last five years both in scope and complexity in similar operating environment. Details of the assignment – Name, Client, scope value and period shall be provided; and
  4. The firm’s overall institutional, managerial, and technical competence and capability to undertake the assignment, in terms of number and appropriate mix of its technical experts, financial strength, institutional quality management system and goodwill in the industry.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers, January 2011 revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

  1. The firm may associate with other Consultants to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

  1. Consultant will be selected in accordance with Quality Cost-Based Consultants (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers, January 2011 revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”)

 

  1. Interested Consultants may obtain further necessary information at the address below during office hours between 0900 to 1600 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400Hrs) and public holidays.

 

  1. The expressions of interest in written form must be delivered in person, or by mail to the address below so as to reach by 21st September, 2021 at 11:00am.  EOI may also be deposited in the Tender Box on Ground Floor, Maji House, Ngong Road and must be clearly marked: “CONTRACT No: KE-MOWI-246482-CS-QCBS for CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO UNDERTAKE AN INVENTORY OF EXISTING RURAL WATER SUPPLY SYSTEMS, O&M INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY AND COMMUNITY WATER VULNERABILITY AND NEEDS ASSESSMENTS IN FIVE ASAL COUNTIES OF KENYA (TURKANA, MARSABIT, MANDERA, WAJIR AND GARISSA)” addressed to:

Contract Title: CONSTRUCTION WORKS FOR THE SECOND BARICHO – KAKUYUNI WATER SUPPLY PROJECT- LOT 1: SECOND BARICHO – KAKUYUNI PIPELINE

Contract No.: KE-CWSB-232660-CW-RFB

1. The Coast Water Works Development Agency (CWWDA) through the Government of Kenya (GoK) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Construction Works for the Second Baricho – Kakuyuni Water Supply Project- Lot 1: Second Baricho – Kakuyuni Pipeline, Contract No. KE-CWSB-232660-CW-RFB.

2. The Coast Water Works Development Agency (CWWDA), a Parastatal under the Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation now invites sealed bids from eligible and qualified bidders (Construction Contractors) to undertake the works i.e. Construction works for the Second Baricho – Kakuyuni Water Supply Project- Lot 1: Second Baricho- Kakuyuni Pipeline. The Works include but are not limited to:

  • Supply and installation of three (3) pump sets (Q=820m3/hr, H=70m) within the existing pump house and associated electromechanical works
  • Excavation, supply and laying of 29Km of DN 800mm steel pipeline
  • Construction of 5,000m3 reservoir at Kakuyuni
  • Testing and commissioning of pumps, pipeline and reservoir

The Contract Period will be Twenty Four (24) months following the date of effectiveness of the Contract, comprising of Twelve (12) months of Construction Period and Twelve (12) months of Defects Liability Period.

3. Bidding will be conducted through the National Competitive Bidding procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Guidelines: Procurement of Goods, Works and Non-Consulting Services under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants by World Bank Borrowers  dated January 2011 and revised in July 2014  (“Procurement Guidelines”), and is open to all eligible bidders as defined in the Procurement Guidelines. and inspect the bidding documents during office hours 0745 hours to 1630 hours local time from Monday to Friday, except during lunch hour (1230 hours to 1400 hours), during weekends and public holidays at the address given below.

6. Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before 1200 hours Local Time on 1st October, 2021. The Government of the Republic of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for consulting services for needs identification and proposal of a working solution for a citizen engagement mechanism (CEM) for WASREB under Component 3 of the project.

 

  1. The Project comprises four components; -
  1. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in the coastal region, - Mombasa, Kwale, Kilifi and Taita Taveta Counties

  3. National performance-based financing (PBF) that includes support for water and sanitation infrastructure investments, and technical assistance for performance-based financing.
  4. Project management to finance the management activities associated with project implementation.

 

 

  1. In line with WASREB’s mandate under section 72(1)(j) of the Water Act, the objective of this assignment is to propose a working solution for citizen engagement as well as provide an avenue for monitoring of this activities by the regulator with the aim of enhancing the citizen voice in the provision of water services. The assignment entails proposing a working solution/mechanism (reporting system, consumer groups etc) for obtaining citizen feedback in service provision.

 

  1. The specific objectives of the assignment are: (i) Identify the current citizen engagement mechanisms and technological trends within utilities and provide a status of the same (ii) Propose a system to assist the utilities and regulator in citizen engagement including a mechanism for grievance redress and (iii) Link the identified citizen engagement mechanisms with WASREB’s requirements.

  1. At least 5 years of experience in the field of marketing, Advocacy, dispute resolution, capacity building and advisory services;

 

  1. Demonstrated experience in development and implementation of citizen engagement mechanisms.

 

  1. An in-depth understanding of the Kenya water and sanitation sector, including an understanding of the regulatory and policy environment.

REPUBLIC OF KENYA

MINISTRY OF WATER, SANITATION AND IRRIGATION

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

COUNTRY: KENYA

NAME OF PROJECT: WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSDP)

PROJECT No.: P156634

CREDIT No. 630 -KE

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:  INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT -  GENDER SPECIALIST

 

CONTRACT REF. No.: MOWSI/WSDP/005/2020-2021 (KE-MOWI-228006-CS-INDV)

 

The Government of the Republic of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for consulting services for Development of Gender Action Plans under Component 2: Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in underserved northeastern counties of Kenya.

 

  1. The Project comprises four components; -
  1. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in the coastal region, - Mombasa, Kwale, Kilifi and Taita Taveta Counties
  2. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in Wajir and Garissa Counties
  3. National performance-based financing (PBF) that includes support for water and sanitation infrastructure investments, and technical assistance for performance-based financing.
  4. Project management to finance the management activities associated with project implementation.

 

  1. The main objectives of this assignment are to: (i) undertake rapid gender audits and consultations on water and sanitation issues in Wajir and Garissa counties; and (ii)support the development and implementation of Gender Action Plans for Wajir and Garissa counties. 

 

  1. Duration of the assignment is 12 Months.

 

  1. Interested candidates can access the detailed Terms of Reference for this assignment on the Ministry’s website: www.water@go.ke.

 

  1. Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation now invites eligible individual consultants to express their interest (EOI) in providing these services. Interested consultants must provide their CVs and information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

 

  1. The desired consultant must be in possession of the following qualifications and experience: -

 

  1. An advanced degree (Master or above) in Sociology, Anthropology, Social Development, Gender & International Studies, International Development or related field;
  2. Proven expertise with minimum eight years’ experience in key disciplines associated with gender, citizen engagement and social development, etc.  Specific experience on gender mainstreaming in the water sector preferable.
  3. Experience in qualitative research tools (interviews and focus group discussion) required.
  4. Extensive knowledge of and work experience within context of gender and social inclusion.
  5. Knowledge of the Kenya water and sanitation sector, and specifically the North-Eastern region, an added advantage.
  6. Demonstrated ability to work as a team member for providing innovative solutions to solve complex technical and development issues.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers, January 2011 revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

procnotices.notice_text:
KWALE WATER AND SEWERAGE COMPANY LTD

P.O Box 18-80403 Tel: 0412014155

E-mail: info@kwalewater.co.kewebsite: www.kwalewater.co.ke

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

COUNTRY:

KENYA

PROJECT:

WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSDP)

Credit No:

IDA- 6030-KE

Assignment Title:

HIRING OF AN ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIAL SAFE GUARDS SPECIALIST

Reference No.

KE-KWAWASCO-225728-CS-INDV

The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consultancy services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include;

Task 1: Project Preparation

  • To screen the subprojects for potential environmental and socio-economic risks and impacts
  • Conduct Environmental and Social Impact Assessment studies and prepare Safeguard Reports and present them to KWAWASCO
  • To review and provide comments on draft Environmental and Social Impact Assessment Reports (ESIA) and ESMP documents (prepared by consultants)

Task 2: Project Implementation, Monitoring and Supervision:

  • Supervise the implementation of the environmental and social management plans (ESMP) for and on behalf KWAWASCO for all the sub-projects under WSDP;
  • Reviewing documentation pertaining to environmental and social compliance (including bidding documents, reviews on-site, reports from contractors etc.) during project implementation;
  • Assess if the grievance redress mechanisms established for the project are functioning appropriately.
  • Assess the major environmental, health and safety non-compliances, incidents and proposes corrective actions with strict timelines;
  • Identify issues to be addressed through the safeguard’s instruments for the project within the context of COVID-19 Pandemic guidelines and review those issues with the consulting firms;
  • Contribute to project progress reports pertaining to overall implementation of environmental and social requirements of the project as requested by World Bank (monthly, quarterly etc.), on progress on environmental safeguards for all sub-projects;
  • Ensure adherence of the social safety measures by the contractors as guided by the Ministry of Health in the containment of COVID-19 Pandemic protocols.
  • Participate in project missions and follow up with the Consultants and ensure the actions agreed by the Joint Implementation Missions of the World Bank and the KWAWASCO are implemented;
  • Participate in incident/accident investigations by project contractors and supervising consultants and subsequent follow-up on agreed action plans;

 

Task 3: Reporting

The Environment and Social Safeguards Specialist will carry out the following:

  • Ensure that ESIAs/ESMPs cleared by the World Bank and NEMA are disclosed in the WSP’s area of Jurisdiction;
  • Review monthly, quarterly and other ad hoc environmental and social safeguards reports submitted by the Consultants and Contractors before submission is accepted by the implementing Agencies i.e. County/KWAWASCO and the Bank;
  • Prepare reports on workshops and field visits, minutes of meetings, and others.

 

Task 4: Management and Training:

  • Support the Project coordination unit in daily management and implementing training and policy activities related to planning and managing the environmental and social safeguards aspects;
  • Prepare training materials and conduct safeguards training workshops to KWAWASCO, the County Government of Kwale and their respective Contractors.
  • Any other duty as may be assigned by the MD KWAWASCO.

 

Kwale Water & Sewerage Company Limited now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The short listing criteria are: 

Qualification and Experience

  • Master’s degree or equivalent related to Social Science (Sociology, Anthropology, orDevelopment Studies) with a deep understanding of the practical aspects of the environmental health and safety issues included in this ToR, or Environmental Studies (Environmental Science, Natural resource management, Envi. Planning, Health & Safety) with a deep understanding of the practical aspects of the social issues included in this TOR, or other technical discipline in social and natural resources management
  • Documented evidence and experience with similar successful assignments corroborated by recommendations of the clients;
  • The staff should be registered with NEMA as a lead expert.
  • Should have accumulated at least Eight (8) years general working experience and 5 years’ previous specific experience on preparation and implementation of ESIA and ESMP for water related infrastructure projects;
  • 3 years’ previous specific experience on supervision of environmental and social safeguards/resettlement action plans implementation on World Bank funded projects;
  • Knowledge and Experience in working with communities and diverse range of stakeholders. The staff should possess excellent oral and written communication skills in English and Kiswahili.
  • Proven ability to function as a team player, to work across institutional boundaries, and to collaborate with other entities. Hands-on and action-oriented approach;
  • Excellent oral presentation skills and written communication skills in English.
  •  Ability to work in an intercultural environment would also be an advantage;
  • Competence with standard MS Office software (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), preferably combined with computerized analytical skills required.

 

Selection Method

Selection of an Individual Consultant will be done in accordance with World Bank’s Guidelines for Procurement under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits dated January 2011, and the Guidelines for Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers dated January 2011.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0900 hours to 1600 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to1400 Hours) and public holidays.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, email or mail) by 3rdJune 2021 at 11.00 am Local Time.

procnotices.notice_text:
COAST WATER WORKS DEVELOPMENT AGENCY (CWWDA)

 

                    

 

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country: Kenya

 

Project: Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP)

 

Credit No.:60300 – KE

 

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Preparation of Final Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) Studies/or Reports and Preparation of   Final Resettlement Action Plans (RAP) for The Proposed Mwache/West mainland and Mwache/North mainland Pipelines

 

 

Reference No: (As per Procurement Plan): KE-CWSB-224323-CS-QCBS

 

 

1. The Government of Kenya has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of the Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) includes carrying out Preparation of Final Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) Study Reports and Preparation of   Final Resettlement Action Plans (RAP) for The Proposed Mwache/West mainland and Mwache/North mainland Pipelines. The consultancy services will take nine (9) calendar months and forty-one (41) staff months. The specific activities include:

  • Desk Review of the Preliminary ESIA and Preliminary RAP reports and other Project reference documents;
  • A concise description of environmental guidelines and standards;
  • Description of the baseline environmental conditions;
  • Subprojects description including geographical, ecological and general layout maps;
  • Determination of potential environmental and social impacts of the subprojects;
  • Measures to mitigate adverse environmental and social impacts of the subprojects;
  • Development of an environmental and social management plan;
  • Conducting Public Consultations;
  • Preparation of Resettlement Action Plan (including LRP and PF if applicable).

 

 

3. The Coast Water Works Development Agency (CWWDA), a state corporation under the Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation (MWS&I), now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. Relevance, competence, and suitability of the applicant firm’s core business to this specific assignment,
  2. Number of active years in the business and the firm’s general and specific contract experiences,
  3. Successful delivery of minimum of two (2) similar nature, complexity, operating context, and sized assignments, within the last recent years,
  4. The applicant firm’s overall institutional, managerial, and technical competence in terms of financial strength, institutional quality management system and goodwill in the industry are also considered during short listing qualified firms for the assignment.

 

Key-experts’ CV will not be evaluated at this stage.

 

4. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 1.9 and 1.11 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants (under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants) by World Bank Borrowers January 2011, revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and eligibility. 

 

5. Consultants may submit their REOI as an individual firm or in association in the form of a joint venture or sub-consultancy.  All the members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment.  However, the experience of sub-consultant will not be considered while short-listing.

 

6. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines.

 

7. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours i.e. 0800 to 1630 hours excluding lunch time 1230-1400 hours’ local time and public holidays.

 

8. Expressions of interest should be clearly marked with the following statements “EoI for Consultancy Services for Preparation of Final Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) Study Reports and Preparation of   Final Resettlement Action Plans (RAP) for The Proposed Mwache/West mainland and Mwache/North mainland Pipelines” and must be delivered in written form to the address below (in person, or by email) by 12th May, 2021 at 1200 hours local time.

 

The Chief Executive Officer,

Coast Water Works Development Agency,

P.O. Box 90417 – 80100,

Mikindani Street, Mombasa.

E-mail: info@cwwda.go.ke and procurement@cwwda.go.ke

Republic of Kenya

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY    :           KENYA

 

PROJECT     :           WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT

PROJECT.

 

IDA Credit No.:        IDA 60300

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:       Consultancy services for Development of Garissa County Water Master Plan.

 

REFERENCE No.: KE-GAWASCO-202394-CS-QCBS

The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments of goods, works, related services and consulting services to be procured under this Project.

One of the components of the Project, Component 2, will finance a program of activities designed to improve water supply and sanitation services in the northeastern counties, particularly the Dadaab refugee camp host communities in Garissa County and Wajir town in Wajir County.

 

Garissa Water and Sewerage Company (GAWASCO) is the implementing agency for the sub-component that will finance water and sanitation services for the Dadaab host communities.

The objective of the consulting services (“the Services”) is:

  1. To develop a Masterplan for Domestic, Livestock and Industrial Water for Garissa County.
  2. To develop an implementation schedule of proposed strategies of the master plan within a period of 25 years in stages of 5 years and this should be in line with the National Water Master Plan
  3. To review and identify potential water source(s) in the county and recommend strategies for their development after consideration of hydrological / geo-technical / social / economic and environmental factors. This will include mapping and assessment of the existing surface and groundwater sources including transmission and distribution networks. This will also include a comparison of life-time cost.
  4. To make recommendations for exploitation of the available water resources
  5. To carry out a comprehensive analysis of Ground and Surface water availability
  6. To prepare water demand estimates domestic, livestock and Industrial) for the county up to the year 2045 and explore any relevant demand management options such as pricing and management possibilities.
  7. To determine the investment needs and prepare investments plan for both short and long term to address the gap in water supply, water balance and focus on growth, with application of appropriate technologies.
  8. To consider and incorporate recommendations of other studies undertaken or being undertaken by other relevant authorities including the County Government of Garissa, Northern Water Works Development Agency, Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation (National Water Masterplan 2030), among others
  9. To prepare detailed feasibility study for all options and preliminary engineering designs for the selected options and detailed designs and tender documents for the best option selected.
  10. To prepare Strategic Environmental Impact Assessment, Social Impact Assessment (including RAPs), hydrological and Geo-technical study reports for the selected options.
  11. To prepare a water resources master plan for the preferred water source(s) based on the development strategies recommended in (a) above.

 

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) is for Development of Garissa County Water Master Plan.

 

Garissa Water and Sewerage Company (GAWASCO) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. Relevance and suitability of the core business area of the applicant firm with the subject assignment;
  2. Firm should have at least five (5) years relevant experience in the field of Capacity Building in Community-Led Total Sanitation Concept (Relevant completion certificates and/or letters of recommendation from clients to be provided)
  3. Firm should have undertaken at least one (1) similar assignment in the last five years both in scope and complexity in similar operating environment. Details of the assignment – Name, Client, scope value and period shall be provided; and
  4. The firm’s overall institutional, managerial and technical competence and capability to undertake the assignment, in terms of number and appropriate mix of its technical experts, financial strength, institutional quality management system and goodwill in the industry.

 

 

The consultancy services will be carried out over a period of twelve (12) calendar months

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants (under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants) by World Bank Borrowers January 2011, revised July 2014 (‘Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub consultancy to enhance their qualifications. All the members of joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire assignment. However, the experience of the sub-consultant will not be considered while shortlisting.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during the office hours 0900 to 1600 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400 Hrs.) and public holidays.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by 6th April 2021 at 10:00 am.

‘‘Contract No. KE-GAWASCO-202394-CS-QCBS - Consultancy services for Development of Garissa County Water Master Plan.”

The Government of the Republic of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for consulting services for the prevention of, and response to, sexual exploitation and abuse within the project areas.

 

  1. The Project comprises four components; -
  1. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in the coastal region, - Mombasa, Kwale, Kilifi and Taita Taveta Counties
  2. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in Wajir and Garissa Counties
  3. National performance-based financing (PBF) that includes support for water and sanitation infrastructure investments, and technical assistance for performance-based financing.
  4. Project management to finance the management activities associated with project implementation.

 

  1. The objective of the assignment is to enhance the capacity of the project to mitigate and manage project-associated risks related to Gender Based Violence (GBV) and Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) between the project workers and the communities within the project zone of influence and Sexual Harassment between personnel/staff working on a given project, and to ensure survivors have access to safe, confidential and ethical services.  Interested candidates can access the detailed Terms of Reference for this assignment on the Ministry’s website: www.water@go.ke

 

  1. The duration of the services is eighteen (18) months.

 

  1. The Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation now invites eligible Civil Society Organizations (“CSOs/Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Due to the unique and exceptional nature of the envisaged assignment, the selection is targeting indigenous not-for profit organizations or Civil Society Organizations (CSOs).  Interested NGOs/CSOs/Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. Have at least 8 years' experience in the design and implementation of SEA prevention and response programs.

 

  1. Demonstrate knowledge of SEA drivers and risk factors in the project area targeting vulnerable groups and development of programming to respond to those drivers and risk factors.
  2. Experience in development and delivery of SEA sensitization and awareness trainings, including trainings targeting community facilitators and members of local structures (e.g. village health teams, local council, religious institutions, traditional leaders, schools)
  3.  Demonstrate experience in the Kenya’s legal, policy and institutional framework for GBV, Child protection and related issues.
  4. Demonstrate to have the necessary staff to execute the assignment successfully including key experts, non–key experts and support staff who will be supported by a competent team at the CSO’s head office. The proposal of the CSO shall present the staffing schedule in a manner that makes it clear as to which personnel will be involved in a specific activity. A staff organogram reflecting the envisioned activities should therefore be presented.
  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers, January 2011 revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

  1. CSOs/Consultants may associate with other CSOs/Consultants to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

  1. CSO/Consultant will be selected in accordance with Quality Cost-Based Consultants (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers, January 2011 revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”)

 

  1. Interested CSOs/Consultants may obtain further necessary information at the address below during office hours between 0900 to 1600 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400Hrs) and public holidays.

 

  1. REPUBLIC OF KENYA

MINISTRY OF WATER, SANITATION AND IRRIGATION

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

COUNTRY: KENYA

PROJECT No.: P156634

CREDIT No. 629 & 630 -KE

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:  INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT -  SANITATION ENGINEER

 

CONTRACT REF. No.: KE-MOWI-213058-CS-INDV

The Government of the Republic of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for consulting services for a Sanitation Engineer.

  1. The Project comprises four components; -
  1. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in the coastal region, - Mombasa, Kwale, Kilifi and Taita Taveta Counties
  2. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in Wajir and Garissa Counties
  3. National performance-based financing (PBF) that includes support for water and sanitation infrastructure investments, and technical assistance for performance-based financing.
  4. Project management to finance the management activities associated with project implementation.           The consulting services include: i) to provide technical and project management support to the Government of Kenya in the implementation of the sanitation sub-components of the project; and ii) to support institutional capacity strengthening on sanitation services delivery by providing specific technical advice, capacity building and guidance on sanitation and sewerage/wastewater operations.

The services will be up to 31st October 2022. However, the Sanitation Engineer shall be engaged on a one-year renewable contract subject to satisfactory performance, availability of funds and continuation of the project.

Interested candidates can access the detailed Terms of Reference for this assignment on the Ministry’s website: www.water@go.ke.

Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation now invites eligible individual consultants to express their interest (EOI) in providing these services. Interested consultants must provide their CVs and information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

 

The desired consultant must be in possession of the following qualifications and experience: -

  1. A first degree in Civil Engineering or equivalent from a recognized university.
  2. A Master's Degree in Sanitary/Sanitation Engineering or Wastewater Engineering or Environmental Engineering or Public Health Engineering.
  3. Must have served as the lead engineer or deputy lead engineer in at least two (2) sanitation projects in the last ten (10) years with a value of at least USD 1 million each of which the combined scope of work for the two projects should include onsite sanitation (containment and collection), faecal sludge management, sewerage network and sewage treatment systems.
  4. Eexperience in working with the public sector and NGOs in delivery of sanitation and sewerage projects.
  5. Working experience on international financing or donor institution assisted projects
  6. Computer skills to include in computer aided design of sanitation and sewer systems and project management software and tools.
  7. Membership of a recognized and relevant professional engineering body

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers, January 2011 revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

The selection criteria will be solely based on individual experience and qualifications.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY.    KENYA

PROJECT.   WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT

CREDIT NO.   60300

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:  CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR DEVELOPMENT AND ROLL-OUT OF SANITATION BEHAVIOR CHANGE COMMUNICATIONS CAMPAIGN.

 

 

REFERENCE NO. KE-WAJWASCO-179682-CS-QCBS

 

The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include consultancy services for Development and roll-out of sanitation behavior change communications campaign.

 

The consultancy services are for a period of 12 months.

 

Wajir Water and Sewerage Company (WAJWASCO) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.  The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  • A minimum of 10 years in consultancy as a core business.
  • Relevant experience in Environmental Sanitation and Hygiene
  • The consulting firm should have experience of successful execution of at least two (2) projects of similar nature both in scope and complexity in similar operating environment in the last five (5) years with at least one (1) assignment in the last three (3) years. Details of the Assignment-Name and address of the client, scope, value and period shall be provided.
  • Provide overall firm’s managerial, technical competence and financial capability to undertake the assignment including an organogram or narrative of the firm. Also showing company's staff compliment

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants (under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants) by World Bank Borrowers (“Consultant Guidelines”) of January 2011, revised July 2014, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub consultancy to enhance their qualifications.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during the office hours 0900 to 1600 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400 Hrs.) and public holidays.

KWALE WATER AND SEWERAGE COMPANY LIMITED

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

COUNTRY:

KENYA

PROJECT:

WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSDP)

Credit No:

IDA- 6030-KE

Assignment Title:

CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION FOR THE PROPOSED UKUNDA URBAN WATER SUPPLY IMPROVEMENT WORKS.

Reference No.

KE-KWAWASCO-161466-CS-CDS

   

The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consultancy services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include;

  1. Design Review based on existing detailed designs, with a particular focus on non-revenue water management and pressure management.
  2. Supervision of the water supply improvement works contracts and implementation of social and environmental safeguards following the project documents, the World Bank Safeguard Policy and Kenya regulations,
  3. During the Defects liability period, the Consultant shall review the operations and maintenance manuals, back-stopping assistance for water supply operator and staff  on job training.

The Project Schedule is thus envisaged as follows:

  • Design review                                                                         2.0 months                                                     
  • Construction Supervision & Works Commissioning              12.0 months
  • Defects Liability Period Inspections                                      12.0 months
  • Final completion inspection and reporting                             1.0 months 

Total Estimated Input                                                         27.0 Calendar Months

 Kwale Water & Sewerage Company Limited now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The short listing criteria are: 

  1. Core business as a consulting firm with at least ten (10) years relevant experience in the field of water supply and sanitation systems (Borehole drilling, Transmission pipeline & Distribution works) covering  feasibility studies, designs, Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), Resettlement Action Plans (RAP) and works supervision;
  2. Demonstration of having been involved in successful execution of at least two (2) projects of similar nature both in scope and complexity in similar operating environment in the last five (5) years with preferably  one (1) in Sub-Saharan Africa and at least one (1) assignment in the last three (3) years. Details of the assignment-Name and address of the client, scope, value, period shall be provided. 

3.  Detailed company profiles highlighting technical capability to undertake the assignment.

4.  Demonstration of availability of knowledge and appropriate skills among key consultant staff.

 The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers January 2011, revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and eligibility.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0900 hours to 1600 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to1400hours) and public holidays.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

COUNTRY    KENYA

PROJECT.    WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT

CREDIT NO   60300

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:  CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR UTILITY     TURNAROUND   FRAMEWORK.

REFERENCE NO. KE-WAJWASCO-154020-CS-QCBS

 

The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Water and Sanitation Development Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services

The consulting services (“the Services”) include consultancy services for utility turnaround framework.  A Utility Turnaround Framework is an approach which helps in designing systematic, coordinated and prioritized interventions for improving operational and managerial capacity. The formulated and prioritized interventions are a result of a sequence of assessments, recommendations and decision steps. In the UTF methodology, five utility-management elements are assessed which are: Organization and Strategy; Human Resources, Financial management; Technical and Commercial operations. Prioritized interventions to improve the performance of the aforementioned 5 utility-management elements are captured in a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP).

 

The consultancy services are for a period of 24 months.

 

 

Wajir Water and Sewerage Company (WAJWASCO) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.  The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Core business as a consulting firm with at least 10 years relevant experience in the field of water supply systems, feasibility studies, designs, EIAs, RAPs and Works supervisions;
  2. Demonstration of availability of knowledge and appropriate skills among key consultant staff.

Demonstration of having been involved in successful execution of at least two (2) similar assignments both in scope and complexity in similar operating environment in the last five years, with at least one initiative in the last three years. CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR a Social and Environmental Safeguards Expert

 

CONTRACT NO: KE-MOWASCO-136307-CS-INDV

 

The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towardS the cost of THE WATER and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds from this financing for the payment of Consulting Services for A SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SAFEGUARDS EXPERT; CONTRACT NO: KE-MOWASCO-136307-CS-INDV

 

  1. The successful attainment of the goals and the efficient delivery of the WSDP will require project commitment; project safeguards policies and documents especially the Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) and to ensure that the WSDP does not detrimentally influence the environment and social well-being of populations. The WSDP - PCU intends to reinforce its capacity in social safeguards with the recruitment of a Social and Environmental Safeguards Expert. 

 

  1.    The Post - reporting to the Project Coordinator, the SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SAFEGUARDS EXPERT will be responsible for the provision of support services for project safeguards policies and documents especially preparation and review of the Resettlement Action Plans (RAP) and to ensure that the Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP) complies with project’s Resettlement Policy Framework and does not detrimentally influence the environment and social well-being of populations.

 

  1. For the detailed Terms of Reference for this assignment with specific objectives and scope of the tasks, key deliverables, timing, competence and qualifications and other requirements, please visit the following website: www.mombasawater.co.ke
  2. Mombasa Water Supply and Sanitation Co. Limited (the client) now invites eligible individual consultants to express their interest (EOI) in providing these services. Interested consultants must provide their CVs and information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services. The desired consultant must have the following skills and expertise:
  1. A degree in social science, anthropology, or a comparable field.
  2. At least 10 years of relevant work experience on World Bank’s funded projects’ resettlement or social issues. 
  3. Direct knowledge of (and experience working with) Kenyan social, land and resettlement laws and regulations.
  4. Experience in preparing/reviewing at least four Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) and Environmental Impact Assessment reports

procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIC OF KENYA

MINISTRY OF WATER & SANITATION AND IRRIGATION

WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSDP)

PROJECT NO.: P156634 CREDIT NO. 629 & 630 -KE

 

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION

 

CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR DETAILED DESIGN, PREPARATION OF TENDER DOCUMENTS, ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT, RESETTLEMENT ACTION PLAN AND SUPERVISION OF CONSTRUCTION WORKS FOR WAJIR LONG – TERM WATER SUPPLY

 

CONTRACT No.: NWWDA-WSDP-03-2019-2020

The Government of the Republic of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for consulting services.

The Consulting Services (“the services”) include: -

  • Detailed designs and associated documents (drawing, bills of quantities, specifications, bidding documents, and safeguards documents) for Wajir Long – term Water Supply.
  • Supervision of the water supply works contracts and implementation of social and environmental safeguards.

The main objective of the assignment is to conduct a technical, social and economic comparative analysis of the two water supply options; - Ademasajida and Arbajahan as proposed in the master plan study for Wajir and develop detailed designs for the preferred option and supervise the implementation of the works.

The duration of the services is expected to be Forty-Two (42) calendar months, i e. twelve (12) months for design stage, eighteen (18) months for construction phase and twelve (12) months for Defects Liability Period (DLP).

The Ministry of Water & Sanitation and Irrigation now invites eligible consulting firms “Consultants” to indicate their interest in providing the consultancy services for detailed designs and associated documents (drawing, bills of quantities, specifications, bidding documents, and safeguards documents) for Wajir Long – term Water Supply and Supervision of the water supply works contracts and implementation of social and environmental safeguards. Interested Consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant comprehensive experience to perform the Services.

The short listing criterial for the firm’s capability and experience are:

  1. Core business as a consulting firm with at least ten (10) years relevant experience in the field of water supply systems covering feasibility studies, designs, Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), Resettlement Action Plans (RAP) and works supervision;
  2. Demonstration of having been involved in successful execution of at least two (2) projects of similar nature both in scope and complexity in the last five (5) years. Details of the assignments shall include; Name and address of the client, scope, value, period and completion certificates and/or letters of recommendation from clients.

KWALE WATER AND SEWERAGE COMPANY LTD

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST
