COUNTRY:

KENYA

PROJECT:

WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSDP)

Credit No:

IDA- 6030-KE

Assignment Title:

Consultancy services for community awareness and mobilization for owner upgrade of urban house hold sanitation facilities in Ukunda,Kwale and Kombani for Kwale Water & Sewerage Company Limited

Reference No.

 

KE-KWAWASCO-74622-CS-LCS

The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds on consultancy services for community awareness and mobilization for owner upgrade of urban household sanitation facilities in Ukunda, Kwale and Kombani under Kwale Water & Sewerage Company Limited

The objective of the assignment is to advocate for upgrading of existing infrastructure on sanitation and hygiene as follows:

  1. Upgrading existing pit latrines;
    1. Lining existing latrines with an impervious slab and with an access for emptying
    2. Investing in disludging pit latrines
  2. Upgrading pit latrines to septic tanks with soak pits;
    1. Households to be persuaded to invest in connecting to the centralized water pipeline mains
    2. Investing in construction of septic tanks and soak pits
    3. Investing in disludging septic tanks and soak pits

To achieve the above goal, the consultancy is expected to involve the following activities:

  1. Social mobilization of property owners’;
  2. Advocacy through appropriate local media in Kwale County in order to strengthen property owners’ awareness, raise the visibility and profile of the issues around risky unimproved toilet facilities and the importance of improved, lined, emptiable pit latrines and septic tanks;
  3. Empowering property owners to make informed decisions on improved sanitation and hygiene based on dissemination of impactful information of the present situation;
  4. Sensitize property owners on the social, environmental and economic benefits accruing from the investment in improved long-term sanitation and hygiene options; and
  5. Development and dissemination of IEC Materials for empowering property owners and decision makers with information they need.

 

The consultancy services will be carried out over a period of 36 calendar months. 

KWAWASCO now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The short-listing criteria are:

  1. Core business as a consulting firm with at least ten (10) years relevant experience in the field of sanitation systems, and in particular, mobilization and or campaign in marketing, health and related activities;
  2. Demonstration of availability of knowledge and appropriate skills among key consultant staff.
  3. Has been involved in successful execution of at least two (2) similar assignments both in scope and complexity in similar operating environment in the last five years, with at least one initiative in the last three years. Details of the assignment - name and contact address of the Client, scope, value, and period shall be provided; and
  4. Appropriate overall institutional, managerial and technical competence.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers (“Consultant Guidelines”) of January 2011, revised July 2014 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub consultancy to enhance their qualifications.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Least Cost Selection (LCS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines.

procnotices.notice_text:
ASSIGNMENT TITLE: Consultancy services for Development of Wajir county Environmental Sanitation and Hygiene Policy & legal documents to Wajir Water and Sewerage Company.

 REFERENCE NO    : KE-WAJWASCO-80986-CS-QCBS.

 

The Government of the Republic of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 The Consulting services (“the Services”) include but not limited to: Development of Wajir county Environmental Sanitation and Hygiene Policy & legal documents in Wajir town.

 The Consultancy services will be carried out as follows:

  • Wajir County Environmental Sanitation and Hygiene Policy;
  • Wajir County Environmental Sanitation and Hygiene Strategic framework; 
  • Wajir County Environmental Health and Sanitation Bill.
  • Wajir County ODF Campaign Framework implementation of WSDP.

 

The consultancy services will be carried out over a period of 30 calendar months.

Wajir Water and Sewerage Company (WAJWASCO) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The short-listing criteria are:

  1. Core business as a consulting firm with at least ten (10) years relevant experience in the field of Environmental Health, Sanitation, Hygiene and Law (Constitutional, Human Rights, Environmental or any other related Law fields).
  2. Demonstration of availability of knowledge and appropriate skills among key consultant staff.
  3. Has been involved in successful execution of at least two (2) similar assignments both in scope and complexity in similar operating environment in the last five years, with at least one initiative in the last three years. Details of the assignment - name and contact address of the Client, scope, value, and period shall be provided; and
  4. Appropriate overall institutional, managerial and technical competence.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants (under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants) by World Bank Borrowers (“Consultant Guidelines”) of January 2011, revised July 2014, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub consultancy to enhance their qualifications. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines.

COAST WATER WORKS DEVELOPMENT AGENCY

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Country: Kenya

Project: Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP)

Credit No.: IDA – 6030 KE

 

Assignment Title: Preparation of Preliminary Designs, Feasibility Study, Detailed Designs, Safeguards Documents and Tender Documents and Construction Supervision of Second Baricho – Kakuyuni Water Pipeline and Transmission Pipelines to Kilifi and Ganda Tanks

 

Reference No.: KE-CWSB-102977-CS-QCBS

 

1. The Government of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the Preparation of Preliminary Designs, Detailed Designs, Safeguards Documents and Tender Documents and Construction Supervision of Second Baricho – Kakuyuni Water Pipeline. The specific activities include:

  1. Feasibility studies of the proposed pipelines by selecting the most feasible routes.
  2. Preliminary and detailed design of the most feasible option.
  3. Prepare tender documents and safeguards documents (in lots) as per the latest World Bank procurement guidelines and assist in the selection of the works contractor.
  4. Fulfil the role of the Engineer’s Representative in construction supervision and management of Environmental, Social, Health and Safety (ESHS) issues.
  5. Provide the Client with regular status reports and other reports as per the Terms of Reference, together with all related necessary technical assistance and professional advice to the Client related to feasibility, design and supervision of the construction of the said works.
  6. Prepare a post construction management and maintenance manuals for the facilities.

 

3. The estimated key expert-input is one hundred and eleven (111) staff months over a period of forty-three  (43) calendar months.

 

4. The Coast Water Works Development Agency now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

    1. Must have a minimum of 10 years in engineering consultancy as a core business.
    2. The consulting firm should have experience in feasibility studies, Preliminary design, detailed design, preparation of tender documents, preparation of safeguards documents and works supervision of major water infrastructures in Africa for the last ten (10) years (experience in East Africa added advantage).
    3. The consulting firm should have experience of at least three projects of similar nature involving engineering studies and works supervision during the last ten (10) years, each with a value of  at least USD 0.5 million.
    4.  The consulting firm should have experience in projects funded by International Financing Institutions (IFIs) such as World Bank, AfD, AfDB (added advantage)
    5. Detailed company profiles including technical capability to undertake the assignments.

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 1.9 and 1.11 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants (under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants) by World Bank Borrowers dated January 2011, and revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and eligibility. 

 

6. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

7. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Consultant Guidelines.

 

8. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0800 to 1630 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1230 to 1400 hrs.) and public holidays.

  • Demonstration of having been involved in successful execution of at least two (2) projects of similar nature both in scope and complexity in similar operating environment in the last five (5) years with preferably one (1) in Sub-Saharan Africa and at least one (1) assignment in the last three (3) years. REPUBLIC OF KENYA

MINISTRY OF WATER AND SANITATION

WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSDP)

PROJECT NO.: P156634 CREDIT NO. 629 & 630 -KE

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FOR INSTITUTIONAL STRENGTHENING AND CAPACITY BUILDING FOR

FOUR WATER SERVICE PROVIDERS (WSPs) IN COASTAL REGION

 

CONTRACT No.: MoWS/WSDP/02/2018-2019

 

The Government of the Republic of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for consulting services. The Consulting Services (“the services”) include provision of qualified Technical Assistance in Institutional Strengthening and Capacity Building to four Water Service Providers in Coastal region.

 

  1. The Project comprises four components; -
  1. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in the coastal region, - Mombasa, Kwale, Kilifi and Taita Taveta Counties
  2. Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in Wajir and Garissa Counties
  3. National performance-based financing to finance construction of new or rehabilitation of existing water and sanitation infrastructure for the WSPs/WSBs, with a specific focus on expanding coverage and improving services.
  4. Project management to finance the management activities associated with project implementation.

 

2. The Project aims at enhancing the operational, commercial and financial performance of participating water service providers through capital investments and measures for improvements of their management and operation. An Initial Institutional Assessment was conducted and a Performance Improvement Program (PIP) Report outlined for four WSPs including Kilifi-Mariakani Water and Sewerage Company (KIMAWASCO), Kwale Water and Sewerage Company (KWAWASCO), Malindi Water and Sewerage Company (MAWASCO) and Taita-Taveta Water and Sewerage Company (TAVEVO) based on the Utility Turnaround Framework (UTF) methodology.

 

3. The goal of the PIP is to enhance the provision of reliable and hygienically safe water supply for the population of the Programme cities with cost covering and socially affordable tariffs as well as provide adequate on site and centralized fecal sludge management. This is to contribute to an efficient use of the water resources and to environmental protection with parallel improvement of living, working and health conditions for the population.

The Objective of the PIP is the improvement of the economic and financial sustainability of the WSPs in order to contribute to sustainable water supply and sanitation services of the utilities.

4. The duration of the services is expected to be initially for three (3) years on time based contracts.

5. The Ministry of Water and Sanitation now invites eligible consulting firms “Consultants” to indicate their interest in providing Technical Assistance in Institutional Strengthening and Capacity Building to four Water Service Providers in Coastal region. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant comprehensive experience to perform the Services.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The short listing -

  1. Have a minimum of 10 (ten) years of core business as a consultant in the areas of Financial Management, Procurement, Safeguards and Civil Engineering
  2. Undertaken a minimum of three (3) similar assignments in the last four (5) years;
  3. Experience in similar conditions in the last five (5) years in terms of the clientele and area of proposed services; and.
  4. Demonstration of technical and managerial skills to undertake the services.

 

6. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers, January 2011 revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

7. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

8. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with Quality Cost-Based Consultants (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants [under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants] by World Bank Borrowers, January 2011 revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”)

 

9. Interested consultants may obtain further necessary information at the address below during office hours between 0900 to 1600 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400Hrs) and public holidays.

 

10. The expressions of interest in written form must be delivered in person, by email or mail to the address below or deposited in the tender box so as to reach by 18th  June 2019. EOI may also be deposited in the Tender Box on Ground Floor, Maji House and must be clearly marked: “CONTRACT No: MOWS/WSDP/01/2018-2019 for CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR INSTITUTIONAL STRENGTHENING AND CAPACITY BUILDING FOR FOUR WATER SERVICE PROVIDERS (WSPs) IN COASTAL REGION” addressed to:

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY        :           KENYA

 

PROJECT         :           WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT

PROJECT (WSDP).

 

LOAN NO         :           60300-KE

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:   CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO ASSIST WASREB IN MANAGEMENT, IMPLEMENTATION AND COORDINATION, MONITORING AND EVALUATION OF THIRTEEN (13) PROJECTS IN ELEVEN (11) WATER SERVICE PROVIDERS IN THE COUNTIES OF NYERI, MURANG’A, KAJIADO, MACHAKOS, UASIN GISHU, NAKURU, NAIROBI, LAIKIPIA AND KIAMBU. 

 

 

REFERENCE NO      :     KE- WASREB- 34809-CS-QCBS

 

 

 

The Government of the Republic of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Water and Sanitation Development Project (WSDP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The WSDP under component 3, (National Performance Based Financing, NPBF) has three windows intended among others to support participating Water Service Providers (WSPs) improve access to water and sanitation services and to improve operational and financial performance based on an agreed set of performance measures with WASREB. Each WSP will be supported by a design and supervision consultant firm. WASREB shall be responsible for reviewing the project proposals and monitoring the general implementation of the projects.

 

The activities include carrying out of programs designed to strengthen the capacity of WASREB to manage, implement and coordinate, monitor and evaluate the projects, including: (i) evaluation of proposals to identify high-return investments and activities; (ii) establishment and implementation of a comprehensive monitoring and evaluation system; and (iii) provision of training to participating counties and water services providers involved in implementation of the program on issues such as implementation of safeguards, procurement and financial management.

 

The Consulting services (“the Services”) include:

 

  1. Providing support to the consultants during the design of the projects;
  2. Ensuring the selected projects are financially self-sustaining on completion;
  3. Participating in site meetings and ensure that bottlenecks that may impede implementation of works are overcome as soon as possible;
  4. Assisting WASREB to undertake effective monitoring of the projects during implementation by ensuring compliance to procedures and adherence to the Terms of Reference;
  5. Providing all necessary technical advice (actions/interventions) to WASREB as may be appropriate to facilitate successful execution of the projects;
  6. Monitoring the project and reporting the progress made and problems faced to WASREB;
  7. Drawing up appropriate action plan(s) for the full implementation of the projects;
  8. Ensuring that the project funds are spent according to the requirements of the funding contract and report any deviations.

 

The projects are thirteen (13) spread in eleven (11) Water Service Providers in the counties of Nyeri, Murang’a, Kajiado, Machakos, Uasin Gishu, Nakuru, Nairobi, Laikipia and Kiambu.

 

The duration of the consultancy services shall be initially for twenty four (24) calendar months.

 

The Water Services Regulatory Board (WASREB) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The short-listing criteria are:

 

  1. Core business as a consulting firm with at least 10 years relevant experience in the field of water supply systems, feasibility studies, designs, EIAs, RAPs and Works supervisions;
  2. Demonstration of availability of knowledge and appropriate skills among key consultant staff.
  3. Demonstration of having been involved in successful execution of at least two (2) similar assignments both in scope and complexity in similar operating environment in the last five years, with at least one initiative in the last three years. Details of the assignment - name and contact address of the Client, scope, value, and period shall be provided;
  4. Appropriate institutional, managerial and technical competence.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants (under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants) by World Bank Borrowers (‘Consultant Guidelines”) of January 2011, revised July 2014 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE (GPN)

KENYA WATER AND SANITATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (WSDP)

Project ID No. P156634

 

The Government of the Republic of Kenya has applied for financing in the amount of US$ 300 million equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Kenya Water and Sanitation Development Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, related services and consulting services to be procured under this project.

The project will include the following components:

Component 1– Rehabilitation and expansion of urban water supply and sanitation services in the coastal region.

Sub-Component 1.1 Support to coastal counties: This subcomponent will provide finance to counties and their WSPs that are connected to the bulk water system for the construction and rehabilitation of water distribution and sanitation systems in urban areas, and for Technical Assistance (TA) to improve their performance.

Sub-Component 1.2 Support to coast bulk water services provider: This subcomponent will support Coast Water Services Board in the rehabilitation, expansion and extension of parts of the bulk water system.

 

Component 2 –Expansion of water supply and sanitation services in marginalized northeastern counties of Kenya.  This component will finance short, medium, and long-term investments to increase access to water and sanitation services in Wajir town and in the communities near the Dadaab refugee camp in Garissa County. Technical Assistance (TA) will also be provided to support the Counties and the WSPs to expand and improve the services. 

 

Component 3 – National Performance-based Financing (PBF)

Subcomponent 3.1: Support for water and sanitation infrastructure investments and activities - This will finance construction of new or rehabilitation of existing water and sanitation infrastructure for the WSPs/WSBs, with a specific focus on expanding coverage and improving services.

Subcomponent 3.2 – Technical Assistance for national performance-based financing (PBF): This sub-component will finance a program of activities designed to strengthen Water Services Regulatory Board’s capacity for management, implementation and coordination, and M & E of the National PBF.

 

Component 4 – Project Management

This component will finance the management activities associated with the implementation support, including establishing and implementing a comprehensive monitoring and evaluation (M&E) system and training of implementing entities on safeguard and fiduciary policies.

Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing (IPF) Borrowers, for Goods, Works, Non-Consultancy Services and Consultancy Services, July 2016.

Specific procurement notices for contracts to be bid under the World Bank’s international competitive bidding (ICB) procedures and for contracts for consultancy services will be announced, as they become available, in UN Development Business on Bank’s External Website (www.worldbank.org) and in local newspapers.

Interested eligible bidders and interested consultants, or those requiring additional information are encouraged to follow announcements on upcoming bidding opportunities or should contact the agencies below.
